outdoor.note: 老松林, laid out as the rooms describe themselves and as their climbs land (DECISIONS「老松林按原文方位排布」): the forest path from Snow (npath1-3) runs south and turns east to the round clearing with the great pine in its middle (clearing); three ways leave it, east, west and south (clearing.c), the sign by the south one, where the straight slope runs down south, high in the north and low in the south (spath1-4, a dead end); east the path to the mossy stone bridge over the gorge that runs south from the waterfall north of the bridge, and the strip at the foot of the cliff beyond it (epath3) with the broken plank road up the cliff (epath3.c: 一条破旧的栈道沿著山壁通往山上). On the high ground east of the gorge the pines close in: pine1-7 and cliffdown are one fixed maze of gaps between the trees (DECISIONS) with a loop, two dead ends and the way on to cliffdown on its west edge, above epath3; from pine1, at the plank road's top, one way south to the cliffside on the same edge, above the gorge, one east to the keep's hidden gate (keep1) and the stockade (keep2: sandbags and stone piles, the stakes; keep3: the bear skin and three chairs, braziers, locked chests, the pit).

gorge.note: The gorge below the bridge: the waterfall pours from the cliff into a chest-deep pool walled in on three sides (waterfall); the stream runs south along the west wall between steep cliffs, the old bridge high overhead (riverbank2), rocks jutting into the water from the east bank where one can stand, and the cliff one can climb (riverbank1); south through the gap where the stream falls in, the bottomless pool ringed by strange grass under sheer walls (lake).

Needle mats along the boughs; empty air all round.
